adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent the fallback branch is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. That `.find(...)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then it compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so it will not match any real calendar externalId and returns `undefined`. Unlike createEvent (which does `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), updateEvent does not show any `|| "primary"` fallback at the call site, so it can pass `calendarId: undefined` to `calendar.events.update(...)`, breaking updates for references without an externalCalendarId (legacy). The same dead-lookup pattern is also present in deleteEvent’s computed calendarId in this diff.
